title: Full research pass review of the geez lane, 2026-10-19
semantics: Project-created review metadata. Versions include witnesses, components, translations and unresolved leads; their count is not a count of substantive revisions. Acquisition does not establish transcription, collation, normative revision or local reception. No ancestry is asserted.

review_files.storage: untracked workspace scratch; pinned here by SHA-256 only

uses.label: Ethiopian Catholic Church
uses.finding: Present book: the joint 2024 edition (alex-geez-2025) replacing 1945. Historical Catholic Ge'ez books: Keren 1890 (unacquired), Asmara 1914/15 (acquired; approved 1913 for priests of the rite received in Abyssinia), Rome 1945 (unacquired). Earlier Catholic use of Ethiopian-rite books is reported for the Paez era and from 1847, without identified books. The 2002 English weekday missal is a deferred translation.
uses.limit: No original 1890 or 1945 book; Ethiopian (as distinct from Eritrean) reception of the Asmara book is not shown by its imprimatur, which is Eritrean.
uses.review_remaining_gap: Ethiopian-territory reception of the 1890 and Asmara books; 1945 original and decree; 2024 approval and implementation; post-1945 Ethiopian Catholic printings; Catholic lectionary.

uses.label: Eritrean Catholic Church
uses.finding: The Asmara book carries the imprimatur of the Vicar Apostolic of Eritrea (12 April 1913) and was printed at the Catholic press in Asmara: direct historical authorization within the predecessor jurisdiction. The 1945 edition has bounded Eritrean reception through the Blin translation (existing record note). The 2024 edition is joint.
uses.limit: Ecclesial separation (2015) creates no new text; post-1915 Eritrean printings of the Catholic book are unsearched.
next_sources: Eparchy of Keren and Archeparchy of Asmara publications
uses.review_remaining_gap: Eritrean reception of 1890 shown only regionally; post-1915 Eritrean printings unsearched; 2024 implementation in Asmara; Blin and Tigrinya translations deferred.

uses.label: Shared historical Catholic Ge'ez use (Vicariates of Abyssinia and Eritrea; Jesuit-era mission)
uses.finding: Book sequence: Paez-era two-anaphora missal (lead), pre-1888 revised anaphoras (lead), Keren 1890, Asmara 1914/15, Rome 1945, joint 2024. The 1890 decree for a Ge'ez Roman rite is a separate, apparently unrealized translation project.
uses.limit: Early stages known only from a reference work.

uses.label: Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Mäṣḥafä qəddase (comparison only)
uses.finding: Rome 1548 print, seventeenth-century and later manuscripts, Addis Ababa printings from 1918 E.C. and Asmara 1993 with Tigrinya are comparison witnesses. None is merged into a Catholic record.
uses.limit: No reception evidence into Catholic books beyond the general statement that Catholic editors used the Ethiopian rite.

versions.label: Aksumite Collection Euchologion, UM-039
versions.date_label: codex 13th century or earlier; translations 5th to 7th century
versions.distinctness_basis: Existing record; early Eucharistic layer including Mark.
versions.unresolved: Unchanged; no Catholic reception.

versions.label: Anaphora of the Apostles in the Senodos and Testamentum Domini strata
versions.distinctness_basis: Component layer named by the EAE article, not a book.
versions.unresolved: Unexamined range: Senodos and Kidan editions; no dated station.

versions.label: Testamentum Novum ... Missale (Rome, 1548; colophon 1549), Ge'ez liturgical section ff. 158r to 176v
versions.distinctness_basis: Earliest printed Ordo communis with three anaphoras (Apostles, Our Lord, Mary by Cyriacus); distinct printed witness.
versions.unresolved: Contents of ff. 175 to 176 and holding copy unidentified; not collated.

versions.label: Petrus Aethiops, Latin rendering of the Ethiopic Mass (Rome, 1549)
versions.distinctness_basis: Latin translation, further Latinized (invocation curtailed, Filioque inserted) per the EAE article.
versions.unresolved: Original not acquired; exact title unverified.

versions.label: Bullarium Patronatus Portugalliae Regum, Appendix (Lisbon, 1879): reprint of the 1548 anaphoras
versions.distinctness_basis: Reprint; not a new textual state.
versions.unresolved: Not acquired.

versions.label: Ge'ez missal used by Ethiopian Catholic priests in Paez's time, reported to retain two anaphoras purged of anti-Chalcedonian wording (Leo named in place of Dioscorus)
versions.date_label: c. 1603 to 1622 (Paez's residence); book date unknown
versions.distinctness_basis: Reported substantive reduction and revision of the anaphoral repertoire and diptychs.
versions.unresolved: No original witness. Unexamined range: Jesuit letters and Beccari volumes, Paez Historia de Ethiopia, Mendes and Almeida; manuscript catalogues for Catholic-revised anaphoras.

versions.label: Paez, Historia de Ethiopia book 2 chapter 11: Portuguese translation of the pre-anaphora and Anaphora of the Apostles (ed. Beccari, Rome 1905, pp. 439 to 453)
versions.distinctness_basis: Translation, kept separate from the reported revised Ge'ez missal.
versions.unresolved: Not acquired.

versions.label: Roman rite in Ge'ez: Mendes's Latinization from 1625 and the decree of 10 July 1890 that the Latin rite translated into Ge'ez replace the Ethiopian rite
versions.distinctness_basis: A Roman-missal translation project, not an Ethiopian-rite book; the NCE says nothing came of the 1890 decision.
versions.unresolved: Whether any Ge'ez Roman missal was printed is unestablished; belongs with Latin-rite translation histories, which are deferred.

versions.label: Ethiopian-rite books used by de Jacobis's Catholic clergy under the permissions of 6 July 1847 and 21 April 1850
versions.distinctness_basis: Use of Ethiopian-rite (manuscript) books; no Catholic edition identified.
versions.unresolved: Books used are unidentified.

versions.label: Thirteen anaphoras revised and considered 'catholic' before 1888 (Vicar Apostolic Touvier)
versions.distinctness_basis: Reported revision of anaphoras preceding the 1889 to 1890 commission.
versions.unresolved: No witness identified; manuscript or lithograph form unknown.

versions.label: Keren Catholic missal, 1890 (fourteen anaphoras)
versions.tradition_or_use: Catholic Ge'ez (Vicariate of Abyssinia, Keren press)
versions.distinctness_basis: Existing record. NCE: Crouzet reported on 8 November 1891 that fourteen revised anaphoras dated 1890 had been printed and circulated without his imprimatur, for interim use.
versions.unresolved: Original not located online; Bonn's catalogue title quotes a Keren 1890 imprint formula for the Asmara book, possibly an earlier-imprint statement not found on inspected pages.

versions.label: ሥርዓተ፡ ቅዳሴ፡ ዘቤተ፡ ክርስቲያን፡ ካቶሊካዊት፡ እንተ፡ በኢትዮጵያ። Asmara, Ethiopian year 1907 (1914/15); approved 25 February 1913
versions.distinctness_basis: Approved as 'rite revisum et mendis expurgatum'; fourteen numbered anaphoras by headings, one ascribed to Dionysius; order of Communion repeated.
versions.unresolved: Difference from 1890 cannot be measured without the 1890 original; not transcribed.

versions.label: Congregatio Orientalis: Documenti relativi al Rito Etiopico I to II (1940); Notationes atque animadversiones de Anaphoris Ritus Aethiopici (1940); Liturgia-Etiopi, Revisione e ristampa del Messale Etiopico, Allegato I to II (1944)
versions.distinctness_basis: Preparatory documents, not altar books; potential evidence for 1945 changes.
versions.unresolved: Documents not located online.

versions.label: Maṣḥafa qǝddāse / Missale aethiopicum, Vatican 1945
versions.distinctness_basis: Existing record; EAE: prepared under van Lantschoot, 17 anaphoras (Apostles, Our Lord, Mary I, Mary II, John the Evangelist, James the Lord's brother, Mark, 318, Athanasius, Basil, Gregory of Nyssa, Epiphanius, Chrysostom, Cyril, Jacob of Serug, Gregory, Dioscorus).
versions.unresolved: Original 1945 book and decree not acquired.

versions.label: Blin translation based on the 1945 Vatican missal (Eparchy of Keren)
versions.distinctness_basis: Vernacular translation; establishes bounded Eritrean reception of 1945.
versions.unresolved: Translation itself not acquired.

versions.label: The Ethiopian Rite Missal for Weekday Celebrations of the Eucharist with seven Anaphoras, English edition ad experimentum (Addis Ababa, 2002)
versions.distinctness_basis: English adaptation by Fritsch and Cogavin; deferred.
versions.unresolved: Not acquired.

versions.tradition_or_use: Catholic Ge'ez, joint Ethiopian and Eritrean

versions.label: Ethiopian Orthodox printed Mäṣḥafä qəddase: Addis Ababa 1918 E.C. (1925/26, first EOTC printing), later Addis Ababa editions including 1926 E.C., 1942 E.C., 1951 and 1957 keys, 1959 with Amharic, 1962 E.C.; Asmara 1993 with Tigrinya

acquisitions.delivered_extent: Whole provider PDF, 181 pages: one ULB Bonn identification sheet plus 180 page images matching the 180 canvases of the IIIF manifest (covers, endpapers, frontispiece, title, Ge'ez permission, Latin approbation, printed pp. 5 to 162, rear endpapers and cover). acquisitions.identity_inspection: Inspected 2026-10-19 on renders made from this file: PDF p. 10 title page (ሥርዓተ፡ ቅዳሴ፡ ዘቤተ፡ ክርስቲያን፡ ካቶሊካዊት፡ እንተ፡ በኢትዮጵያ። Imprint: ተኀትመ፡ በሀገረ፡ አሥመራ፡ በማኅተመ፡ ካቶሊካውያን፡ በ፲፱፻፯ ዓመት፡ እምልደተ፡ እግዚእነ። The imprint numeral reads ፲፱፻፯, Ethiopian-reckoning year 1907, which Hammerschmidt and the Encyclopaedia Aethiopica both equate with 1914/15). PDF p. 12 Ge'ez permission (መባሕት) dated 25 Yakkatit and 1913 by Roman reckoning, signed for the Congregation by Cardinal Gotti and secretary Rolleri. PDF p. 13 Latin approbation: the Missale Aethiopicum according to the rite received in Abyssinia, described as duly revised and purged of errors, approved and permitted to be printed for priests of that rite, Rome, Propaganda Fide pro negotiis Ritus Orientalis, 25 February 1913; imprimatur Asmara, 12 April 1913, Fr. C. Carrara, Vicar Apostolic of Eritrea. PDF p. 175 printed p. 162 ends with a doxology and no colophon. Flyleaf shelf notes read Goussen 1665. Section starts by PDF page (Bonn structural ranges, headings read on page images): 14 ሥርዓታት፡ ወጸሎታት፡ (preparatory orders and prayers); 22 ግብዓተ፡ ግብር፡ ዘቅዳሴ፡ (order of the service, reading of first word uncertain); 40 Anaphora of the Apostles; 50 ሥርዓተ፡ ተመጥዎተ፡ ቍርባን፡ (order of Communion); 56 no. 2 Our Lord; 66 no. 3 Our Lady Mary; 74 no. 4 John son of Thunder; 84 no. 5 the 318 Orthodox; 94 no. 6 Athanasius; 104 no. 7 Basil; 112 no. 8 Gregory of Nyssa; 118 no. 9 Epiphanius; 126 no. 10 John Chrysostom; 132 no. 11 Cyril of Alexandria; 138 no. 12 Dionysius, great archbishop of Alexandria; 150 no. 13 heading ዘደብረ፡ ዘይት፡ ወዘጳጕሜን፡; 158 order of Communion repeated; 164 no. 14 Gregory of Armenia. Headpiece numerals were read at reduced resolution; the anaphora attributed elsewhere to Dioscorus is headed for Dionysius here. The prior researcher also viewed PDF pp. 5, 7 to 13 and 178 at full resolution.

expected_list_reconciliation.expected_label: Asmara Catholic Ser'ata qeddase, catalogued as second edition, 1907/1913
expected_list_reconciliation.evidence: The frozen dating conflict is resolved on the book itself. Full-resolution IIIF crop of the title page (canvas 3222919) reads the imprint Asmara, Catholic press, year ፲፱፻፯ 'from the birth of our Lord'; the fifth glyph is the zeta-derived seven. The Ge'ez permission leaf dates the Roman approval 25 Yakkatit 1913 'according to the reckoning of Rome', so the unqualified title year is Ethiopian reckoning, 1914/15, as Hammerschmidt (printed p. 19) and the EAE also state. Bonn's 1907 is that Ethiopian year read as Gregorian and its 1913 is the approval year. One book, not two editions; no separate 1913 impression is evidenced.

Update adds the EAE description (van Lantschoot; 17 named anaphoras). The frozen 17/18 conflict is not carried by the packet: the Enciclopedia Cattolica (vol. VII, 1951, p. 782, re-fetched by the cold reviewer) reports 18 anaphoras for the Rome 1945 book. Correction preserves the disagreement.
